title: Disk full because log rotation stopped
symptoms: Disk /var/log is 98% full and keeps growing until 'No space left on device'. The disk never clears by itself; logrotate last ran days ago and old log files are not deleted.
root_cause: logrotate is broken or disabled (bad config, failed cron), so log files grow without limit until the disk fills.
impact: When the disk hits 100% services cannot write logs or temp files and may crash or stop accepting requests.
fix_steps: Find the biggest files: du -sh /var/log/* | sort -h | tail.
Compress or delete old rotated logs (*.1, *.gz) to free space immediately.
Run logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf and check its output for errors.
Fix the logrotate config or cron/systemd timer so it runs daily.
prevention: Monitor logrotate success, cap log size per service, and ship logs to Loki instead of keeping them locally.
